name: Powkiddy RGB30

models.name: RGB30
models.notes: Single model; vertical (clamshell-like) form factor, dual TF card slots

summary: Powkiddy's 4-inch RK3566-based handheld with a square 720×720 vertical display and dual TF-card design (TF1 for OS, TF2 for games). Boots open-source Linux from SD; stock card is the whole system, so a replacement OS is a card swap and going back to stock is a card write.
openByDesign: the OS lives on the TF card, so KNULLI and ROCKNIX boot from a written card with no unlock

specs.storage: TF card only (TF1 for OS, TF2 for games); TF1 supports 16–256 GB, TF2 supports 16–256 GB

variants.notes: Vertical clamshell-style design. Dual independent TF-card slots (TF1 for OS, TF2 for games). 720×720 4.0-inch OCA full-fit screen. Built-in Wi-Fi 5G + Bluetooth. Battery life claimed 8 hours, 2 h charge. 1W×2 cavity loudspeaker. Power input: 5V/2A via USB-C. Console weight 207 g, dimensions 145×86.5×18 mm.

specs.storage: TF1 for OS (16–256 GB), TF2 for games (16–256 GB)
specs.battery: 4100 mAh Li-polymer, 8 h claimed, 2 h charge

firmware.version: Powkiddy stock firmware (system on TF card; Powkiddy lists 'a variety of open source linux')

homebrew.name: KNULLI
homebrew.firmware: Per-model image (knulli-rk3568-powkiddy-rgb30); boots from SD card with no stock-firmware dependency.
homebrew.summary: Batocera-based retro gaming OS for the Powkiddy RGB30. Boots from a prepared SD card; leaves the stock card untouched.

compatibility.note: KNULLI Scarab provides knulli-rk3568-powkiddy-rgb30 image. KNULLI wiki page documents device as RK3566 with Rockchip BSP 4.19 and Mali GL driver.

requirements: A computer with an SD card reader and an image writer (Rufus, balenaEtcher or dd).
warnings: KNULLI ships a separate image per model; cross-flashing does not boot.
Never let Windows format the partitions it cannot read after writing the image.

homebrew.name: ROCKNIX
homebrew.firmware: Per-model RK3566 image; boots from SD card.
homebrew.summary: Mainline-Linux retro gaming OS for the Powkiddy RGB30. Boots from SD card.

compatibility.note: ROCKNIX lists the RGB30 as a supported RK3566 device.

requirements: A computer with an SD card reader and an image writer.
warnings: ROCKNIX ships a separate image per model; cross-flashing does not boot.
Never let Windows format the partitions it cannot read.

homebrew.name: Batocera.linux
homebrew.firmware: SD card image (Batocera 43.1 handheld build); written to an SD card.
homebrew.summary: Batocera.linux's own handheld build, the upstream project ROCKNIX and KNULLI derive from. Written to an SD card.

compatibility.note: Batocera 43.1's handheld download list names 'RGB30'. The page gives the download only, not install steps.

requirements: A device from Batocera's handheld download list.
A computer with an SD card reader and an image writer.
warnings: Batocera publishes a separate image per device; check the exact row before writing.

homebrew.name: spruceOS
homebrew.firmware: Frontend on top of the stock OS.
homebrew.summary: Custom Python-based frontend that runs on top of the stock OS on supported devices.

compatibility.note: spruceOS lists the Powkiddy RGB30 with 'Stable' support status (checked 2026-10-29).

requirements: A new branded microSD card (do NOT use the stock card).
warnings: spruceOS is a frontend, not a full OS replacement; it runs on top of the stock OS.

homebrew.name: Powkiddy stock firmware
homebrew.firmware: Stock system on TF card; restore by writing the stock image.
homebrew.summary: Powkiddy's own OS image on the TF card. Restoring the stock card restores the factory system.

compatibility.note: The stock OS lives on the TF card; nothing inside the device is overwritten.

requirements: The stock TF card or a freshly flashed one from Powkiddy.
warnings: Remove any third-party OS card before booting stock to avoid accidental boot into KNULLI/ROCKNIX.
